title: proj ignore
text:
Commands for interacting with tracking file exclusions, handling operations to manually or automatically modify .gitignore and .Rbuildignore files.


Manually appends one or more raw file or directory paths to the project ignore files.
Unlike automatic configurations driven by _proj.yml, these manual entries represent permanent, user-specified exclusions and are placed strictly above the # --- PROJ MANAGED --- blocks.



<PATHS>...: One or more raw file or directory paths to be ignored.
--force-create: Boolean flag (default true). If true, creates ignore files if they don’t exist. If false, skips file creation unless inherently warranted by environmental cues (e.g. finding a .git folder or a DESCRIPTION file).
--type: Optional filter selection (all [default], git, rbuild). Determines which tracking surface receives the manual path entries. Note that .Rbuildignore is skipped entirely if no DESCRIPTION file exists at the project root.





Manually forces paths to be tracked by appending negated syntax (e.g. !path/ or ^!pattern$).
These unignore entries represent permanent, user-specified negations and are placed strictly below the # --- END PROJ MANAGED --- boundary in .gitignore and .Rbuildignore files.



<PATHS>...: One or more raw file or directory paths to force tracking.
--type: Optional filter selection (all [default], git, rbuild). Determines which tracking surface receives the negated entries. Note that .Rbuildignore is skipped entirely if no DESCRIPTION file exists at the project root.





The library core automatically synchronizes ignore rules dynamically across .gitignore and .Rbuildignore based on the configuration of _proj.yml.

Note: While the automated ignore synchronization is invoked implicitly by the CLI via commands like proj yml read (and acts seamlessly under the hood), the ignore subcommand namespace exists openly to support explicit manual additions via proj ignore add.




The tool automatically locates the project boundaries via a heuristic upward path traversal. It begins checking from the user’s current working directory upward: - It discovers the conceptual root by finding a directory containing a VERSION file. - It continues upward through up to 5 directory levels seeking an optimal foundational root confirming the presence of either _proj.yml or a .git tracking context alongside the VERSION.



The tool targets specifically two core exception list files: - .gitignore (safeguards git commit environments) - .Rbuildignore (safeguards strict CRAN environments and rbuild processes)
Based on the individual block ignore settings within _proj.yml (e.g. ignore: all), properties are intelligently resolved as standard git glob patterns and Rbuild regex match patterns appropriately.



Modifications made by the tool into .gitignore and .Rbuildignore are safely strictly demarcated with protected slice logic block comments. This preserves user-defined modifications outside the managed span: - Operations scan for # --- PROJ MANAGED --- and # --- END PROJ MANAGED ---. - Targeted slice elements are swapped or appended into existing scopes only between these exact markers. - If the boundary blocks are absent, the tool automatically injects them natively at the base end.

title: proj build
text:
The build pipeline script execution engine for the project.
This command evaluates what files need to be run based on configuration layout parameters (build.scripts in _proj.yml) or filesystem auto-discovery. It sorts them according to strict engine precedence rules, modifies format-specific configuration templates when necessary, and executes each script inside its own independent, isolated subprocess.



--major, --minor, --patch: Specifies the version bump strategy for a production build.
--profile: An optional profile to configure execution context.
--description: An optional description string for the build commit. If omitted during a production build that involves git commits, the CLI will interactively prompt for a one-line description when running inside a valid terminal session.





Pre-flight Dependency Checks: Before modifying files or triggering git snapshots, the build engine statically resolves targets to identify dependencies. Depending on the matched scripts (such as .Rmd, .qmd, or .py) and configuration files, it asserts the availability of Rscript (verifying required R namespaces like rmarkdown or bookdown), quarto, or python executable commands. Any missing R packages can be resolved automatically via the PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL environment variable, or through an interactive terminal prompt.
Production Build Restrictions: Checks if branch rules (only_branches, not_branches) or upstream synchronicity (not_behind) are violated during a production build run.
Remote Export Pipeline: During the post-build phase, conditionally exports resolved local target outputs into a deduplicated Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) vault as defined via build.dest targets in remotes.local.
System Git Provider Abstracted: Git mutations safely resolve through a strictly encapsulated host System Git adapter, securely avoiding hanging inputs and ensuring older systems correctly push mutations.
Mutual Exclusion Checking: Before executing, proj build checks for project-level configurations (_quarto.yml and _bookdown.yml). If both exist and the build targets include Quarto or RMarkdown documents, it throws an error to prevent conflicting rendering.
Explicit Execution (Path A):

Define exact scripts, exclusions (starting with !), or sub-directory globs in _proj.yml under build.scripts.
Can rewrite _quarto.yml or _bookdown.yml configuration if specific subset documents are requested.
Maintains order relative to Python and R scripts, while correctly clustering and executing project documents together.

Fallback Execution (Path B):

If no build.scripts is provided, the engine auto-discovers build targets.
Will execute a Quarto project if _quarto.yml exists, or a Bookdown project if _bookdown.yml exists.
Otherwise, it falls back to a shallow workspace sweep and runs .qmd, .Rmd, .R, and .py files in that strict order.





Every resolved file or project rendering task runs inside its own completely independent subprocess, isolated via environment profiles (PROJR_PROFILE) and correct working directory assignments (current_dir), preventing memory leaks and state pollution across execution runs.



proj build-dev
Development runs execute the existing script selection with development Git settings disabled. The CLI does not create or update VERSION, update ignore files, clear released output or previous caches, promote rendered documents into docs, or export to configured local archives. These rules apply on success and failure, even when production configuration enables cleanup, commits or export.
Scripts should explicitly write preview artefacts into their declared cache or staging locations. A subprocess is not a filesystem sandbox: scripts, hooks and renderers can still write where their own code/configuration directs them. Renderer configuration rewriting and script working-directory behavior retain their existing semantics. This change does not introduce automatic output redirection, recursive discovery or a new project-root policy.



build.scripts: [] selects no analysis scripts. Hooks still run, and production builds can version and export existing artefacts as an upload-only workflow. Analysis cleanup, renderer setup and document promotion are skipped so those existing artefacts are preserved. The CLI does not discover scripts instead.
For previews, an absent dev.scripts inherits build.scripts; dev.scripts: [] overrides it with no analysis. Hooks still run, but previews never publish.

title: Command exit status
text:
Successful CLI commands return exit status zero. Reported operation failures return a nonzero status and a diagnostic on stderr, including configuration/path queries, version reads/writes, ignore updates and initialization. Argument parsing errors also return nonzero.
For example, a malformed _proj.yml makes proj yml read --project demo fail, so a shell or frontend can stop instead of treating the diagnostic as success. Failed Git staging, commits and GitHub creation propagate as initialization errors; a failed remote inspection does not proceed to GitHub creation.
This defines success versus failure, not stable error codes, a JSON result schema or a capability protocol. Diagnostics remain human-readable text. Commands may perform work before failing; a nonzero status is not a rollback guarantee.


proj build-dev --project demo --non-interactive
--non-interactive disables the CLI’s own prompts and automatic R-package installation, including when PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL=true. Missing dependencies produce an error. Script, hook and renderer runners and controlled R dependency probes receive closed stdin. The mode is inherited by managed children as PROJ_NON_INTERACTIVE=true.
Initialization still performs requested operations using its existing defaults. This flag does not choose project markers, change configuration precedence or define a structured result protocol. Third-party code remains responsible for its own behavior after receiving EOF.

title: Future R wrapper: CLI installation and CRAN checks
text:
Status: design direction recorded on 2026-10-20, not a shipped wrapper or an accepted CRAN submission. The existing R package remains untouched. This note does not settle the complete frontend protocol or claim renderer parity.


The future wrapper is intended to contain R code that calls a separately installed proj CLI. Its DESCRIPTION should declare that CLI in SystemRequirements. It should discover a compatible executable and give an actionable missing/incompatible-CLI error. A user-invoked installer on the user’s own machine is distinct from automatic downloads during CRAN installation, checks or examples. Do not assume CRAN servers already provide proj.
CRAN source-package policy permits downloads of precompiled software only as a last resort with CRAN-team agreement. A separate executable is not an automatic exemption. Review Writing R Extensions: portability when implementing the package, including external software availability and portable invocation. This work has neither requested nor obtained CRAN agreement; no outreach is authorized here.










Environment
Required behavior




CRAN, CLI absent
Always run meaningful R-only validation, argument construction, missing-CLI diagnostics and mocked protocol/response tests. Skip only genuine executable integration tests, explicitly because the CLI is unavailable.


CRAN, compatible CLI available
Run the applicable real integration tests as well as the R-only tests. Do not assume every check host supplies it.


Our integration CI
Install an exact pinned CLI release, verify its checksum and compatible version, and run real end-to-end tests. Missing CLI or failed installation is a failure, never a silent skip.



Mocked responses check the wrapper contract; they do not prove the CLI or renderer works. Our mandatory integration job supplies that evidence. Examples and vignettes must also handle optional executable availability honestly instead of requiring an undeclared download. A requirement to execute proj on CRAN check servers would need an agreed deployment/checking arrangement, not an assumed policy exception.



The pinned Quarto R package DESCRIPTION at v1.5.1 declares the separate Quarto command-line tool in SystemRequirements. Its test helper can skip executable-dependent tests when Quarto is unavailable, and its vignette utility checks executable availability during vignette processing. These are specific implementation precedents, not proof that CRAN has accepted a future proj wrapper or guaranteed an executable on every server. This note does not infer automatic binary-download permission from Quarto’s existence.
Before implementation, specify compatible protocol versions, executable discovery, argument quoting, diagnostics, and which tests are unconditional versus executable integration. R production changes require separate authorization.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
The behavior contract owns current product decisions. This log records comparison evidence, implementation differences and gaps. Update it in every focused PR; do not infer runtime parity from similar source or green Rust CI.
Relationship labels are same, different, new, and unverified. Each entry states whether that label concerns documented intent, static source, or executed behavior. No comparative R runtime tests have been run for the entries below. Local R/Docker workloads have not been run.



R baseline: SATVILab/projr at 3ac2959.
Thesis baseline: design at b110da5.
Rust pre-migration baseline: 024589b.

New comparisons must pin source commits and relevant files, record the decision and rationale, link executed tests, and distinguish approved, implemented and unverified behavior. Changing a reference baseline does not silently change the product contract.




Relationship: unverified runtime parity; same documented intent. The R README and thesis design describe development previews separately from publication. This is evidence of intent, not proof that every R development path is inert.
Decision/rationale: keep CLI-managed release/version/archive changes out of previews so researchers can inspect development results without publishing.
Implemented: PR123, merged 5d145293e596c5797e9620bd3f00978fa6f99411; Dev-gated VERSION writes, cleanup, document promotion, local export and ignore updates in build.rs, env.rs and yml.rs.
Executed evidence: three-platform Rust tests, including test_preview_safety.rs, and installer checks passed on reviewed head 5d3ac227f52b33fd0c32fddd479cb7296c4072a5. A disposable installed-CLI Python fixture reproduced the previous version/output/ignore mutations.
Gaps: cooperating Python scripts only; renderer YAML rewriting, automatic output isolation, repeated runs, same-project concurrency and full production lifecycle behavior were not established. Subprocesses are not a sandbox.





Relationship: new explicit contract; renderer parity unverified. R path.R dynamically discovers a root, while the thesis defines the project workflow.
Decision/rationale: current approved behavior supersedes defects and stale architecture claims. Root/path defaults must agree across projr, quarto::quarto_render() and RStudio QMD Render. Quarto root equals proj root; nested Quarto projects are unsupported. Direct rendering does not imply release lifecycle parity; R Markdown Knit is a separate entrypoint.
Implemented: PR124, merged 635aa9efac0d7a28971236ab78c879b21be5ec31, corrected AGENTS/README/flow guidance and added the behavior contract. This was documentation, not renderer code.
Executed evidence: independent document review and remote Rust CI passed at dbf8d5fd94a87bba32ffc95cd2ee3b47f1e04277.
Gaps: no direct R frontend, Quarto/RStudio GUI or fresh-render-session parity test was performed. No projr production code or thesis text was changed.





Relationship: different root-resolution mechanism; new CLI selection. R path.R calls root discovery from current context. The CLI now captures one absolute root and passes it to each managed child as PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT.
Decision/rationale: explicit selection wins, and path queries must not change projects after cwd changes. This deliberately improves unstable root behavior rather than copying it.
Implemented: PR125, merged f265eb46c91a300fe0aafad3119d998038946a0b; project.rs, ignore.rs, main.rs and build.rs. Direct library builds configure each child command instead of mutating the caller’s process-global root.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at 779b3010040eeb23f08434478e0812173eb2a723 cover explicit precedence, spaces, invalid roots, changed cwd and overlapping builds in two distinct roots.
Gaps: marker discovery was not changed; R path helpers and direct render entrypoints do not yet consume this captured context. The tests do not promise general environment isolation or same-project concurrent builds.





Relationship: same static read-only configuration intent; runtime R parity unverified. R yml.R reads/merges configuration; this does not establish equivalence of every R public path helper or its cache routing.
Decision/rationale: reading configuration or paths must not update ignore files. Mutating build/init operations request synchronization explicitly, and bad configuration must not replace custom ignores with default rules.
Implemented: PR126, merged cd34c3208f1ed1c3c27571e7ce2828498a4aecdb; yml.rs, build.rs, init.rs/main.rs.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at cc132f1e1b288c7560ff6b6b06fcac369a475355 snapshot files/directories for CLI queries, exercise direct API reads and production ignore synchronization, and preserve custom ignores on malformed/read-failing config. Permission-denied coverage ran on Linux/macOS.
Gaps: supported aliases, unknown-option handling and effective merged script/hook configuration remained unchanged and incomplete.





Relationship: new CLI transport contract; same failure-reporting intent. R build-engine.R uses R errors; that is not a process exit-code protocol for language wrappers.
Decision/rationale: a printed error must not be returned as successful execution. Failed Git remote inspection must not proceed to GitHub creation.
Implemented: PR127, merged 8e955b32bc1f611d38a8931d489de2bdfc50d5c7; main.rs routes operation failures to nonzero status and init.rs propagates previously swallowed external failures.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at a741b5f9de63dcb96ca527607105e5547be1da7c cover failing queries/version/init/ ignores, missing executables, child failure and successful queries. Local fake Git/GitHub commands on Linux/macOS made no network requests.
Gaps: structured error/capability protocols and clean/idempotent Git-init coverage remained open; failure status is not rollback or R-runtime parity.





Relationship: new CLI mode. The R baseline’s build-engine.R calls dependency helpers; no equivalent explicit CLI flag/parity is claimed.
Decision/rationale: machine invocations must not need the CLI’s prompts or automatic package installation. Controlled child stdin must actually be closed.
Implemented: PR128, merged f7ff7e92451a3174d6cb9c5fd60151621e66bd04 after independent review at 5dedee7da69cbe52837993e86bc4837c4c3342a1; adds the flag, inherited mode, runner stdin closure and controlled R-probe stdin closure.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests and installer checks passed at that head; fake-R EOF/no-install tests ran on Linux/macOS and Python runner-stdin coverage ran on all three platforms.
Gaps: no actual R startup/renderer execution comparison; initialization retains existing requested-operation defaults and third-party code can ignore EOF. This does not establish general subprocess isolation.





Relationship: same absent-dev fallback; different explicit-empty guarantee. R yml-scripts.R falls back when dev scripts are absent. Empty-list behavior also passes through validation and renderer selection, so a reliable R upload-only no-analysis contract has not been demonstrated.
Decision/rationale: explicit [] selects no analysis, preserving hooks and production upload/export; absence still falls back. It must not discover or render unrequested files. Cleanup/promotion must preserve upload inputs.
Implementation status: PR129 removes the Dev-empty error and derives one analysis-selection guard for renderer setup/cleanup/promotion. tests/test_empty_scripts.rs checks hooks, existing output/docs bytes, actual production archive bytes and preview nonpublication.
Executed evidence: three-platform Rust tests and installer checks passed at f4b3739554dc548911019c450ca1e90a196d33d2; independent review inspected those logs and cleared that code head. The documentation-only final head 999b730fd2cc23215e4a07a1231d7d6fa3543966 passed all nine checks in runs 39486028024/39486028097 and independent review. Merged as 5617a6daed1f4743a9b2609694a2f84ad4c902eb; post-merge test, installer and site runs 39486858711/39486858532/39486858701 passed.
Gaps: YAML null-as-absence and malformed-list validation were inspected in source, not newly exercised by this policy slice. No R runtime empty-list parity test or real renderer execution is claimed.
Confirmed but separate runtime gaps: retain projr markers (including README/ VERSION), accept legacy _projr.yml with a both-base-files error, and use local > profiles > base with earlier profiles first. The R precedence evidence is yml.R. These approvals are recorded in the behavior contract; this change does not implement aliases, marker expansion or merged script/hook context.




The actual .agents/skills/ponytail/SKILL.md is vendored unchanged from DietrichGebert/ponytail v4.10.0, upstream commit e3ba2aa6f1e6f0bc4d69eb09c9f0d0a93af56156, as installed by PR121. Its pinned upstream bytes and the existing projcli, projr, setupmjr and projects copies all have SHA-256 1316a2f3f95741d2300b116fe0c2d81ce4a9568656ed0a62643f54aaf09957f2. The established setupmjr vendoring contract matches; no duplicate or replacement skill was installed.
The skill prescribes the full-mode simplicity ladder, tracing callers before changing shared behavior, reusing existing code/stdlib/dependencies, and leaving an appropriate runnable check. It supplies no separate executable review script. Applying that guidance is a self-review, separate from independent review and CI.
Completed-chunk review of PR128 at 5dedee7da69cbe52837993e86bc4837c4c3342a1:

Traced the prompt helpers, main description prompt, dependency probes, install branch, script/hooks and project-render runners. Reused the existing EnvGuard, one shared mode predicate and standard-library null stdin; no dependency or custom execution framework was introduced.
Finding/action: the R package probe also needed closed stdin before package detection. That path was corrected and covered by a live-input/fake-R EOF test. Rechecking all controlled status/output paths found no further necessary change.
All three remote Rust suites and installers passed; this self-review remained separate from the independent exact-head review.

Completed-chunk review of PR129’s empty-selection change:

Reused the existing explicit-list resolver and pipeline; no new execution framework, configuration key or dependency was added.
Traced preflight, version, cleanup, hooks, document promotion and publication. Finding: skipping script execution alone could still erase upload-only inputs or require unused renderers. Action: derive one shared analysis-selection guard and apply it before those stages; keep hooks/publication outside that guard.
Retained data-preservation and failure handling. Added runnable integration checks for real archive bytes and absence-versus-empty semantics; those checks passed on all three remote platforms at the code head recorded above. No R runtime parity was inferred.

Decision/rationale: retain those markers with nearest-wins; remove Rust’s VERSION-first/five-extra-ancestors heuristic. Add pyproject.toml and Julia Project.toml/JuliaProject.toml as requested language extensions. Proj config files also anchor a configured project without VERSION. At code head a0d459c5b3a31437443832436535b70d34838553, all nine checks passed in runs 39487247962/39487247928. Independent review compared the pinned marker sources and inspected all three platform logs, clearing that head. Symlink normalization was source-inspected, without a new dedicated test. Final evidence-only head 55e5606e7916f78de7dfb03a4bb43b0ae1a87987 passed all nine checks in runs 39487685152/39487685131 and independent review; merged as 41bd7000363f34b1e7e2d7e354971bfe9021e2b1. title: Proj Build Execution Flow
text:
This page records the existing proj build / proj build-dev implementation. It is not a normative behavior specification. The behavior contract records confirmed decisions and known gaps; current defects do not override it. The build pipeline is designed to enforce structural integrity, version control, and reproducible execution environments. The process is strictly divided into three sequential stages: Pre-Build, Actual Build, and Post-Build.


The pre-build stage focuses on validation, environment auditing, and preparing the workspace state prior to executing any project code.


The _proj.yml configuration is parsed and validated based on the execution mode (development vs. production). The configuration audit also strictly evaluates arbitrary nested keys inside the parameters block and throws a validation error if multiple aliases (parameter, params, param) are found to prevent mapping conflicts.



If the configuration mandates version control integration (git.commit is true): - The system resolves the GitProvider based on the configured engine (config.git.engine defaults to auto or system) and verifies that Git is installed and available on the system PATH. If remote operations like fetching or pushing are necessary and config.git.use_proj_cred_helper is enabled, the credential discovery engine attempts to resolve GitHub tokens. - A check is performed to ensure the Git profile (author identity) is properly configured for the workspace.



The engine resolves scripts and hooks and detects Quarto/Bookdown configuration before version initialization, cleanup, hooks or snapshots. Preflight then checks the production Git restrictions and the interpreters required by those targets.

Production Git checks inspect branch restrictions, tracking remotes and upstream state when configured.
Rscript and required rendering namespaces are checked when needed. The current implementation can offer or perform R package installation; this is existing behavior, not a statement of the future dependency policy.
Quarto availability is checked when needed.
The Python executable is resolved when Python targets are present.




The current version is read from VERSION, with DESCRIPTION and a default version as fallbacks. Development previews do not persist a missing VERSION.



Production builds clear pre-build caches and output directories according to clear_output (pre, post, or never) and may purge old cache versions. Development previews skip these CLI-managed cleanup stages.



Production builds apply --major, --minor or --patch, reset the development flag and write VERSION. Development previews do not bump or write VERSION.



Configured pre and both hooks run after the preceding preparation, before the Git pre-snapshot. Failures propagate from these hooks.



When production Git commits are enabled, the engine commits the pre-build workspace with the “Snapshot pre-build” message.




The actual build stage handles the isolation, resolution, and execution of scripts and documents. This entire stage is executed within a catch_unwind block to safely trap panics and allow for graceful recovery.


The system inspects the workspace for the presence of _quarto.yml and _bookdown.yml. - Mutual Exclusion Check: The presence of both configuration files simultaneously results in a fatal validation error if the build.scripts configuration is omitted or includes documentation targets (.qmd or .Rmd).



The engine determines which scripts to execute based on two possible paths:


During development builds (BuildMode::Dev), the dev.scripts configuration array overrides the standard build.scripts. An explicitly empty array ([]) selects no analysis scripts. It does not fall back to production scripts or discovery; hooks still run.
If target scripts are defined in _proj.yml: - Glob patterns are resolved to absolute paths. - Exclusion patterns (prefixed with !) filter the matched lists. - Empty lists skip analysis, renderer setup and analysis cleanup/promotion, while hooks and normal production publication/export remain available. Preview publication remains disabled. - Documentation files (.qmd, .Rmd) are segregated from standalone scripts (.R, .py). - Dynamic Configuration Updates: If documentation targets are specified, the respective project files (_quarto.yml or _bookdown.yml) are dynamically updated to only render the explicitly requested targets.



If no explicit scripts are defined: - The system determines if it should trigger an automated Quarto or Bookdown site render based on the presence of their configuration files. - If neither exists, a shallow directory sweep is performed, executing discovered files strictly in the order of: .qmd, .Rmd, .R, .py.




The existing implementation starts interpreter subprocesses (for example, Rscript, python, quarto) with current_dir set to the target script’s parent directory. This is a known gap against the confirmed root-relative execution default, not a compatibility requirement. Renderer evaluation directories need their own supported controls. A subprocess does not provide a filesystem sandbox or guarantee a clean environment.
When Quarto or Bookdown configurations are active alongside explicit scripts, a strict reordering constraint is applied: 1. Pre-scripts: All .R or .py files listed before the first documentation file are executed. 2. Doc Clusters: The documentation project render engine (quarto render or rmarkdown::render_site) is triggered. 3. Post-scripts: All .R or .py files listed after the first documentation file are executed.
Otherwise, scripts are executed sequentially exactly as resolved.




The post-build stage acts on the final status of the actual build stage, finalizing version control, syncing remotes, or safely rolling back the workspace.


If the entire build pipeline executes without error and Git integration is enabled (git.commit is true): - A final commit is generated capturing all build artifacts and modifications. - The commit message is formatted as Build v<VERSION> or includes an optional user-provided description (Build v<VERSION>: <DESCRIPTION>).



For production builds configured with clear_output: post, the engine cleans up post-build deployment folders. Additionally, temporary document rendering artifacts (docs/) are automatically cleaned up on successful completion of a single document rendering engine.



After the actual build stage completes successfully and the final Git commit is generated, any configured post or both automation hooks (either build.hooks or overriding dev.hooks) are executed in isolated subprocesses.



For production builds with targets in build.dest and remotes.local configured: - The system iterates over the defined build.dest targets. - Resolved content directories mapped to these targets are piped to the Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) engine. - The CAS engine handles deduplicated storage synchronization, exporting project files into the remote vault.



If Git integration is enabled (git.commit is true) and pushing is configured (git.push is true): - The GitProvider commits the automated workspace build update (capturing compiled asset tracking or CAS mutations). - The GitProvider pushes the local branch mutations to the remote host. - If remote authentication is required and the credential helper is enabled (config.git.use_proj_cred_helper), the CLI securely injects the discovered GitHub token.



If the build pipeline returns an error or panics mid-execution: - Production Rollback: If the build was a production run (--major, --minor, or --patch), the version modifications performed in the Pre-Build stage are reversed. The system restores the pre-build version configuration and ensures the development flag (dev) is set to 1 to maintain safety. - The underlying error is propagated to the CLI output, terminating the process with a non-zero exit code.

If the entire build pipeline executes without error and Git integration is enabled (git.commit is true): - A final commit is generated capturing all build artifacts and modifications. - The commit message is formatted as Build v<VERSION> or includes an optional user-provided description (Build v<VERSION>: <DESCRIPTION>).



For production builds configured with clear_output: post, the engine cleans up post-build deployment folders. Additionally, temporary document rendering artifacts (docs/) are automatically cleaned up on successful completion of a single document rendering engine.



After the actual build stage completes successfully and the final Git commit is generated, any configured post or both automation hooks (either build.hooks or overriding dev.hooks) are executed in isolated subprocesses.



For production builds with targets in build.dest and remotes.local configured: - The system iterates over the defined build.dest targets. - Resolved content directories mapped to these targets are piped to the Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) engine. - The CAS engine handles deduplicated storage synchronization, exporting project files into the remote vault.



If Git integration is enabled (git.commit is true) and pushing is configured (git.push is true): - The GitProvider commits the automated workspace build update (capturing compiled asset tracking or CAS mutations). - The GitProvider pushes the local branch mutations to the remote host. - If remote authentication is required and the credential helper is enabled (config.git.use_proj_cred_helper), the CLI securely injects the discovered GitHub token.



If the build pipeline returns an error or panics mid-execution: - Production Rollback: If the build was a production run (--major, --minor, or --patch), the version modifications performed in the Pre-Build stage are reversed. The system restores the pre-build version configuration and ensures the development flag (dev) is set to 1 to maintain safety. - The underlying error is propagated to the CLI output, terminating the process with a non-zero exit code.

title: Configuration _proj.yml
text:
The _proj.yml file dictates the structural map of your project. It configures the foundational paths and mapping logic used by the CLI.


Custom directory labels are strictly validated against a set of foundational prefixes: - cache - raw - output - docs
These prefixes are case-insensitive. Any label defined in the configuration must begin with one of these approved identifiers.



If you omit the path key for a valid label, the system applies default paths dynamically based on the label prefix: - cache defaults to _tmp - raw defaults to _raw - output defaults to _output - docs defaults to docs
Furthermore, if any of the base prefixes are completely absent from the _proj.yml configuration block, they are automatically injected as default base targets.



The system performs strict validation on _proj.yml: - If a defined directory label uses an unsupported prefix layout, a validation error string will be returned and execution will fail. - All references must resolve correctly; otherwise, the CLI will output an error detailing the structurally invalid labels or malformed content.



The _proj.yml file supports a top-level config block for project-wide settings:

config.git.engine: The Git execution engine to use. Can be auto (default) or system. This determines how the CLI interfaces with Git capabilities natively.
config.git.use_proj_cred_helper: Boolean (defaults to true). Enables the project’s internal GitHub token discovery and credential injection for required remote Git operations. It evaluates sources in strict order (Environment variables GITHUB_PAT/GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN, system Git credential helper, and GitHub CLI) to securely override credentials per-command and prevent freezing on interactive prompts.




The _proj.yml file supports a top-level parameters block for arbitrary nested parameter evaluation. This allows you to define custom metadata and deeply queried values throughout your execution environment.
The configuration engine also supports several aliases for this block: parameter, params, and param. However, multiple alias conflicts within the same configuration file are structurally rejected during validation to prevent mapping confusion.



The _proj.yml file supports a top-level remotes block, which currently supports a local mapping of standalone storage vaults.

local: A mapping where keys represent remote titles and values configure the vault:

path: The physical absolute or relative path to the remote storage directory.
structure: Specifies the storage structure algorithm. Must be cas (Content-Addressable Storage).
content: An array of string tags (matching foundational prefixes or defined directories) specifying which project output directories to sync into the remote upon build completion.
inspect: Specifies the structural integrity verification strategy (manifest or file).





The _proj.yml file can also contain a build block to configure the behavior of the proj build and proj build-dev execution engine. The build block supports the following sub-keys:

dest: An optional list of remote target strings. These targets must be mapped to explicit configurations within the remotes.local block. During post-build execution, resolved content directories matching these tags are piped to the CAS engine for deduplicated storage synchronization.
scripts: An optional list of explicit script paths or glob patterns to execute during the build pipeline.

Globbing patterns are supported.
Prefix a pattern with ! to exclude matching files from execution.
When provided, execution strictly follows the resolved relative order of scripts, bypassing automated project discovery fallbacks unless mutually exclusive configuration states are detected.

hooks: An optional map of lifecycle hook scripts to execute.

pre: Scripts executed before the actual build phase and Git pre-snapshot.
post: Scripts executed after the finalized post-build Git commit.
both: Scripts executed during both pre and post phases.

profile: An optional environment profile identifier. When set, the system injects the PROJR_PROFILE environment variable into the isolated subprocess for all executed scripts and project rendering commands. This can be overridden at runtime via the --profile CLI flag.
git: An optional Git integration configuration. This can be a boolean toggle or an object mapping out detailed toggles:

commit: Whether to automatically perform pre and post-build commits (defaults to false).
push: Whether to automatically push a successful build commit to the remote repository (defaults to false).

restrictions: Configuration block to enforce Git checks specifically during production builds:

only_branches: A list of allowed branch names. Production builds will abort if the current branch is not in this list.
not_branches: A list of restricted branch names. Production builds will abort if the current branch is in this list.
not_behind: Boolean (defaults to true). If enabled, production builds will verify that the local branch has an upstream tracking remote and is not behind it, aborting if the local branch needs to pull upstream changes.

clear_output: An optional string controlling workspace clearing routines for output directories. Can be set to "pre", "post", or "never". If omitted, defaults to evaluating the PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT environment variable.




You can define a dev block to completely override specific configurations during development builds (proj build-dev).

scripts: A list of script paths or globs. During development builds, this array entirely overrides build.scripts. Providing an explicitly empty array ([]) results in a strict error to prevent silently running an empty development build.
hooks: A mapping identical to build.hooks. When specified, these completely replace build.hooks during a development build.
old_dev_remove: Boolean flag. When true, enables purging of legacy cache versions during development builds to save disk space.





PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL: During the proj build pre-flight checks, if required R packages (like bookdown or rmarkdown) are missing, this environment variable controls remediation. If set to true, packages are automatically installed. If absent or set to false, the tool defaults to an interactive terminal prompt (if available) or fails hard.

title: Project and execution behavior
text:
This is the product behavior contract. Confirmed decisions below guide implementation; they are not claims that the current CLI already implements them. Proposals require review before they become requirements. The compatibility log records pinned projr comparisons, decisions, actual test evidence, Ponytail reviews and remaining gaps; update it with each PR.



A project is one analysis/build unit anchored at a selected root directory. It has settings, version information and named resource paths where applicable. Resource paths may be outside the root; a project need not be a Git repository.
Explicit project selection overrides discovery and selects that exact directory.
Automatic discovery walks upward from the invocation directory. The nearest recognized project root wins, including when projects are nested. Discovery does not search downward for projects.
Retain existing projr root markers, including standalone VERSION and README, VCS roots, R-package/RStudio/renv/Quarto project markers, and extend recognition for pyproject.toml, Project.toml and JuliaProject.toml. Proj configuration files _proj.yml / _projr.yml also identify a root. requirements.txt and Manifest.toml alone do not. Recognition must no longer require VERSION before considering the other markers.
_proj.yml is the primary base configuration. Accept _projr.yml as a legacy alias and fail clearly if both base files exist; do not silently merge them.
Configuration precedence follows projr: local overrides profiles, profiles override base, and earlier-listed profiles win conflicts with later ones.
Missing dev.scripts falls back to build.scripts. An explicit empty list in either selects no analysis scripts and never triggers fallback/discovery. Hooks still run; production version/publication/export behavior remains available for upload-only workflows. Development previews never publish. Analysis cleanup and promotion are skipped when no analysis is selected, preserving upload inputs.
With no recognized marker, discovery falls back to cwd. This does not waive build validation: builds require an active root-level proj configuration. The agreed _proj.yml / legacy _projr.yml names apply; explicitly activated profile files may supply configuration, but inactive profile files alone do not. No-config build assumptions from the initial roadmap are superseded.
Every framework/resource directory used at runtime must be explicitly declared. Initialization may write familiar projr defaults into configuration; runtime must not synthesize missing directory mappings or unknown subpaths.
Unsupported behavior-affecting configuration fails before mutations.
Failed supported builds must restore pre-build state except permitted cache residue. This is required behavior, not an implemented transaction guarantee.
Storage/publication retries must have an upload-only route without rerunning analysis or falsely recording a new analysis. Explicit-empty analysis supports hooks/publication, but full retry identity/transaction semantics are separate.
The existing R package is entirely off limits in this effort. Direct R frontend integration is later work; no existing helper changes or parity claims follow from these Rust changes.
Default script/document enumeration is shallow at the selected project root. Subdirectory targets require explicit selection or renderer project configuration.
Scripts execute relative to the project root by default. Selecting a script in a subdirectory does not, by itself, select a different project or execution root.
The resolved root is captured for the run. Path helpers, including a future frontend’s projr_path_get(), resolve against that root even if a renderer or user script changes its working directory.
A supported Quarto project’s root must equal the proj root. Nested Quarto projects beneath that root are unsupported for now. Nested document files are distinct from nested Quarto projects.
QMD rendering through projr, quarto::quarto_render(), and RStudio QMD Render must agree on evaluation directory and root-helper semantics. R Markdown Knit is a distinct entrypoint and must be verified separately. Shared project configuration and direct-entry root resolution are required; CLI-only flags or a parent process environment cannot establish this parity.
Direct rendering does not imply the build, version, commit or archive/export side effects of a proj-managed build.
Renderer evaluation roots must use supported renderer controls. Setting only the parent process cwd is insufficient. Root identity and evaluation cwd remain separate concepts; document asset/reference resolution is not redefined here.

The project root is the analysis workspace’s top-level directory, not the user’s operating-system home directory. Resolving a named resource path is also distinct from changing cwd or selecting a new root.




Apply the base filename compatibility rule consistently to profile/local files and define the effective profile-list source once for config and environment.
Evaluate Quarto execute-dir and R Markdown knit_root_dir / knitr root.dir for root-relative execution. Define the shared persistent configuration and direct-entry initialization before broad renderer changes; do not add nested Quarto project support or rely only on flags passed by proj.
Frontend transport/bindings and remaining environment/YAML compatibility details must be explicit. Familiar projr directory defaults belong in init-generated configuration only; Rust’s _raw and synthesized raw/data runtime paths are not acceptable substitutes for undeclared directories.




The core root finder implements nearest-recognized-ancestor discovery without a VERSION prerequisite. Its marker tests cover the retained projr patterns and deliberate Python/Julia/proj-config extensions and cwd fallback. Required active configuration, explicit directory mappings, early unknown-setting rejection and full failure restoration still need implementation; historical passing fixtures do not demonstrate those new requirements. Individual scripts currently start in their parent directory. Captured-root stability is implemented for core CLI child queries after cwd changes, including independent simultaneous roots; direct R frontend/renderer parity remains unimplemented. Base-file aliases and first-wins profile merging are implemented in configuration reads; build script/hook selection still requires migration to that same merged context. Profile/local filenames retain their existing _projr- form for now. Explicit empty script selection now skips analysis while preserving hooks and production publication; its tests cover production archive bytes and preview nonpublication without invoking real renderers.
Verify nested projects, explicit selection, paths containing spaces, shallow default enumeration, explicit subdirectory scripts, changed cwd, and each supported renderer’s evaluation root. Compare the same nested QMD through projr, quarto::quarto_render(), and RStudio QMD Render; test R Markdown Knit separately. Reject a nested Quarto project clearly. Verify that direct rendering leaves proj-managed release/version/export state alone. Use tiny fixtures and remote CI where practical. Subprocess execution is not a security sandbox, and path hashes alone do not establish scientific correctness or a reproducible environment.



The R wrapper/CRAN design note records separate CLI installation, unconditional R-only tests, conditional CRAN executable tests and mandatory pinned/checksummed executable integration in our CI. It is future design, not a shipped wrapper, CRAN approval or automatic-download permission.

Load and validate configuration without modifying the project:
proj yml read [--project <PATH>]

title: proj version get
text:
Get the project version based on the VERSION file.


The command searches upwards from the current directory to discover the project root containing the VERSION file. It parses the version text (supporting both raw strings like v1.0.0 or JSON objects) and resolves it to a standard output.
If the VERSION file is missing, the tool attempts to fall back and parse the version from an R package DESCRIPTION file if one is present in the project root. If neither a VERSION file nor a DESCRIPTION file exists, it defaults to a newly initialized v0.0.1.
proj version get





Omits the ‘v’ prefix from the output string.
proj version get --no-v



Specifies the output format: - text (default): Outputs the version as a standard string identifier. - json: Outputs the version as a serialized JSON object, detailing its properties (major, minor, patch, and optionally dev).
proj version get --format json




When using --format=json, the output consists of the separated standard semantic components: - major (integer) - minor (integer) - patch (integer) - dev (integer, optional, indicating build cycles or pre-release versioning)

title: proj path get
text:
Get the resolved absolute path for a given label in the project.
proj path get --label <LABEL> [--project <PATH>]


The path resolution mapping dynamically takes the target label and computes an absolute path to the sandbox resource.

Exact Matches: First, the CLI checks if the provided label perfectly matches an existing block declared inside your _proj.yml. If there is a direct match, the declared path rule is applied.
Prefix Nesting Fallbacks: If an exact match is missing, the tool attempts to gracefully interpret the label via a foundational prefix fallback. It identifies if the target begins with an approved foundation (cache, raw, output, docs).

Suffix mappings are appended logically to the base directory. For example, if raw is naturally mapped to _raw, invoking a non-declared label raw-data safely resolves as a direct nested directory, constructing the path _raw/data.





Output path labels securely route into versioned target sandboxes during an active project build. The tool guarantees the resolution produces verified absolute paths directly pointing to their intended source locations, enforcing standard separation across testing segregations and pure-function results.



--project PATH selects that exact existing directory, including a folder without configuration or VERSION. It overrides both ancestor discovery and an inherited run root. Invalid directories fail with a nonzero exit status.
The CLI captures an absolute root as PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT for the invocation and its child processes. A nested proj path get uses that root even after a script changes cwd. An invalid inherited root fails rather than falling back silently. Direct Rust build_project(root, ...) calls also pass their supplied root to children. See the discovery rules below for the recognized root markers.
This establishes CLI child-query behavior, not direct Quarto/RStudio parity or changes to the existing R frontend. Renderer configuration, execution cwd, resource links and output placement remain separate concerns. Path queries do not write ignore files or create the resolved target directories.



Without --project or an inherited run root, discovery walks upward from cwd and selects the first recognized directory. It does not search downward for projects. Recognized markers are VERSION, README.md, _quarto.yml, _proj.yml, legacy _projr.yml, Git/SVN metadata, a DESCRIPTION containing Package:, an RStudio .Rproj whose first line starts Version:, and a renv.lock with a Packages map.
pyproject.toml, Project.toml and JuliaProject.toml deliberately extend the projr marker set for Python/Julia. requirements.txt and Manifest.toml alone are not root markers. Standalone VERSION and README markers are retained, so a nested directory with one is the nearer project; explicit selection overrides it.

The path resolution mapping dynamically takes the target label and computes an absolute path to the sandbox resource.

Exact Matches: First, the CLI checks if the provided label perfectly matches an existing block declared inside your _proj.yml. If there is a direct match, the declared path rule is applied.
Prefix Nesting Fallbacks: If an exact match is missing, the tool attempts to gracefully interpret the label via a foundational prefix fallback. It identifies if the target begins with an approved foundation (cache, raw, output, docs).

Suffix mappings are appended logically to the base directory. For example, if raw is naturally mapped to _raw, invoking a non-declared label raw-data safely resolves as a direct nested directory, constructing the path _raw/data.

--project PATH selects that exact existing directory, including a folder without configuration or VERSION. It overrides both ancestor discovery and an inherited run root. Invalid directories fail with a nonzero exit status.
The CLI captures an absolute root as PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT for the invocation and its child processes. A nested proj path get uses that root even after a script changes cwd. An invalid inherited root fails rather than falling back silently. Direct Rust build_project(root, ...) calls also pass their supplied root to children. Without --project or an inherited run root, discovery walks upward from cwd and selects the first recognized directory. It does not search downward for projects. Recognized markers are VERSION, README.md, _quarto.yml, _proj.yml, legacy _projr.yml, Git/SVN metadata, a DESCRIPTION containing Package:, an RStudio .Rproj whose first line starts Version:, and a renv.lock with a Packages map.
pyproject.toml, Project.toml and JuliaProject.toml deliberately extend the projr marker set for Python/Julia. requirements.txt and Manifest.toml alone are not root markers. Standalone VERSION and README markers are retained, so a nested directory with one is the nearer project; explicit selection overrides it.
